analysis.title: Market Monitor, Week Ending November 20, 2026
key_insights: US equities fell sharply in the week to 11/20: S&P 500 -8.57%, Nasdaq Composite -9.99%. The sell-off was attributed to higher-for-longer rate worries weighing on AI capex, doubts about AI returns, and positioning unwinds that spread across all sectors.
Europe and North Asia fell hard. STOXX 600 -5.78% (worst week since March), KOSPI -7.95% on fears of tighter US semiconductor export controls, TOPIX -6.78%.

Fed October minutes: almost all participants see further hikes as likely appropriate even though the Fed held in October. Two participants, including Waller, said a 50bp hike may be needed in December. Officials expect inflation to fall quickly in 2027 as the energy shock fades.
Fed officials flagged AI as a source of inflation and financial instability, citing rapid growth of AI-related debt in 'complex and opaque financing structures'.
Treasury yields fell on safe-haven demand despite hawkish Fed talk. 2Y ended at 4.65% and 10Y at 4.94%. The 2-10 slope is 0.30%. Bund 10Y 3.30%.
Oil fell on supply surplus expectations, stronger Middle East exports and rising US inventories. WTI ended at $83.98 and Brent at $92.57, down from $104.12 and $117.64 at end of October.
Gold had its worst week in eight months at $3,538.49/oz. A stronger dollar and forced liquidation of gold positions as equities sold off drove it.
Dollar index +0.38% on the week. EURUSD 1.0968, USDJPY 158.57 after PM Takaichi suggested the BOJ may intervene to support the yen.
US data: October retail sales +0.2% MoM in line, core retail +0.6% vs 0.4% consensus. Jobless claims 203k vs 197k consensus. UK CPI 3.6% YoY, highest in a year. Japan Q3 GDP -0.1% vs +0.3% expected.

GSAM's view is to stay the course in US equities. The odds of positive S&P 500 returns rise from 54% over one day to 81% over one year. It expects further equity upside from resilient growth and strong earnings.

AI thesis: GSAM argues the debate is shifting from proving the technology to proving the economics. It cites Anthropic IPO, with about 80% of usage on newest models and $100k+ customers rising from 1,500 in Dec 2025 to 11,900 in Sep 2026.

Nvidia: after Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, GSAM says near-term AI infrastructure demand is intact. Circular financing is small versus a $10-15T AI infrastructure opportunity over six years. Share shifts would change slices, not the pie, and may help rival chip designs.
Bitcoin fell 15.19% on the week, -23.94% MTD and -33.22% YTD. VIX is up 85.96% on the week.
Credit spreads widened: US HY 367bps vs 340 at end Oct, IG 96bps vs 90, EMD 236bps vs 206.
Upcoming: PMIs 11/23, PCE and GDP 11/25, FOMC 12/9, ECB 12/17, BOJ 12/18.

market_movers.rationale: GSAM says Huang's resignation as CEO raises long-term questions but near-term AI infrastructure demand is intact. Rival chip designs may benefit from roadmap uncertainty.

sector_views.rationale: GSAM says tech pullback is normal volatility and expects equity upside from strong earnings, though active selection is needed between AI winners and laggards.
Energy is the best YTD S&P sector performer at +30.2%, but oil is falling on supply surplus expectations.

macro_indicators.interpretation: In line with consensus after +0.8% in September, so consumer demand is holding up.
Above the 0.4% consensus, which supports the hawkish Fed case.
Above the 197k consensus but still low.
Highest in a year, driven by record fuel prices.
Contraction versus 0.3% expected growth, as high energy prices weigh.
Fed on hold in October with hike bias.

crypto_views: Bitcoin fell 15.19% on the week, -23.94% MTD and -33.22% YTD, in line with the broad risk-off move.
risk_factors: Higher-for-longer rates and possible 50bp December Fed hike weigh on AI capex.
AI-related debt in opaque financing structures flagged by Fed as a financial stability risk.
Energy price shock keeping inflation elevated.
Nvidia leadership transition and circular financing concerns.
Buildout limits from permits, power and data center restrictions.
charts_described: Chart of the Week: frequency of S&P 500 rolling periods with positive returns (1970-2026) rises from 54% at 1 day to 81% at 1 year and 100% at 15 years.
Anthropic customers spending at least $100k over 12 months: 20 in Dec 2023, 200 in Dec 2024, 1,500 in Dec 2025, 11,900 in Sep 2026.
vol_and_positioning: VIX rose 85.96% on the week, 84.81% MTD and 140.07% YTD.
Positioning unwinds accelerated the equity sell-off and broadened it across all sectors.
Forced liquidation of gold positions occurred as equities sold off.
geopolitical: Ongoing tensions in the Middle East were outweighed by supply surplus expectations in oil pricing.
Fears of tighter US semiconductor export controls pressured the KOSPI.
UK government urged the public to stock up on emergency supplies, lifting food retail sales.
Japanese PM Takaichi suggested the BOJ may intervene to support the yen.

tension_points.bull_case: GSAM says volatility is normal, the macro backdrop is supportive and strong earnings should drive further equity upside, so investors should stay invested.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher-for-longer rates may weigh on AI capex, returns on AI investment are uncertain, and the Fed flagged opaque AI debt financing as a stability risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 50bp Fed hike at the December 9 FOMC or tighter US semiconductor export controls would challenge the stay-the-course view.

theme_stances.key_argument: Volatility is normal, odds of positive returns rise with horizon, and growth and earnings remain strong.
theme_stances.evidence: investors should stay the course and harness the power of compounding

theme_stances.key_argument: Near-term AI infrastructure demand is intact despite Nvidia CEO change, and circular financing is small relative to the opportunity.
theme_stances.evidence: we believe the near-term outlook for AI infrastructure demand is intact
